purpose: Human-labeling score guide for the fresh unseen semantic-relevance evaluation.

4.label: Strong
4.definition: Directly and strongly matches the central semantic intent of the query; an obvious/direct recommendation.

3.label: Good / Clear
3.definition: Clearly relevant overall, but one important aspect is secondary, implicit, weaker, or missing.

2.label: Partial
2.definition: Meaningfully satisfies one central part of the query but misses another; there is substantive overlap.

1.label: Weak / Incidental
1.definition: There is a genuine requested concept or close equivalent, but it is peripheral or incidental; the book is not really about the request.

0.label: None
0.definition: No meaningful evidence of the requested intent, or the description contradicts it. Speculation is not evidence.

tie_break_rule: When genuinely between adjacent scores, choose the lower score unless the higher score is clearly supported.
evidence_rule: Use the supplied description as primary evidence. Title/author may support interpretation but must not substitute for missing description evidence. Do not use external knowledge.
